races.name: Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Varzi
runners_data.note: Unbeaten juvenile stepping up sharply to 7f from 6f, with wins on good ground only; K.R. Burke in good form (T14: 13/42) and the favoured stall 3 draws helps, but this trip on soft is a significant question mark for a horse whose two runs have been quick-ground sprints.

runners_data.name: Kach Above
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back 7f handicaps in good ground form and clearly handles the trip; Rowan Scott takes the ride and the low stall 1 is a draw advantage, though a 49-day absence and trainer's flat 14-day strike rate (0/20) warrant caution around fitness sharpness.

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: Prominent runner named a danger by the Strand Scorecard and brings solid 7f experience; sim-going record of 1 from 5 with no wins or places on soft is a red flag for today's conditions, and dropping back from recent placed efforts at 7f on good ground means the going switch is the key variable to resolve.

runners_data.name: Engraved
runners_data.note: Very lightly raced — just one run, a 8f second on good ground — making today's step to 7f on soft a considerable step into the unknown; the Fanshawe yard is ticking along (T14: 4/17) and Daniel Muscutt rides, but the lack of experience makes assessing his chance speculative.

runners_data.name: Forbidden Fire
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 6f on good ground for Andrew Balding, who fields in good form (T14: 12/58), but Oisin Murphy has to overcome stall 8 on a track where high draws are disadvantaged; the step to 7f soft is untested and he remains very lightly exposed.

runners_data.name: Rock Montreal
runners_data.note: Roger Varian debutant winner over 7f on good ground (stall 7, AGAINST draw), making the step into Listed company significant; the draw is unhelpful and he has no soft-ground evidence, though Varian's handling of unexposed types is noteworthy.

runners_data.name: Nabati
runners_data.note: Top of the Strand Scorecard at high confidence, rated OR 104 and clearly the class act in the field; William Buick rides for Appleby and the form reads 1-2-1 over 6f, so the step to 7f soft is the only uncertainty, though this hold-up performer's finishing kick is his primary weapon and the race shape must deliver enough pace to suit.

runners_data.name: Minkaas
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 6f on good ground from stall 9 (AGAINST) and all three runs have been at 6f; the jump to 7f soft is a significant distance query, and while the trainer (T14: 0/4) is quiet, Tom Marquand's experience in holding horses up could help in a race where the hold-up profile needs the pace to be honest.

runners_data.name: Vega King
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, ideally positioned from low stall 2 (FAVOURED) to stride straight to the rail; his recent form reads 4-1-0 and that last zero — a last-of-ten — is a concern, though the 8f win in his history suggests stamina for 7f and his tactical position makes him a key race-shaper regardless of his own winning prospects.

races.paceDynamic: Vega King is the sole confirmed front-runner and, breaking from stall 2 on the favoured left rail, he is well positioned to stride into an uncontested lead from the off on this flat, straight Doncaster seven-furlong track. With no serious rivals likely to challenge him for the front early — Dandyman Dan and Engraved are prominent types but neither is a natural leader — Vega King will be able to control tempo on soft ground, meaning the pace is likely to be honest but measured rather than truly searching. Nabati (stall 4, neutral draw) races from hold-up, as does Minkaas, and both will need the pace to be genuine enough to set up their late runs; if Vega King dictates a moderate gallop the race could increasingly suit those tracking closely rather than those coming from the deepest position. This race shape — a single uncontested leader dictating a sustainable tempo on soft ground — most favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can sit just off the pace and produce a sustained finishing effort, with pure hold-up horses reliant on the front-runner not getting away too cheaply.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vega King Dictates, Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If Vega King leads without serious challenge and sets a steady-to-honest pace that winds up evenly through the final three furlongs.
scenarios.body: Vega King controls the race from the front and the field strings out on soft ground behind him, with midfield and prominent runners travelling comfortably before delivering sustained runs; the gallop is genuine enough to expose any front-runner who flatters to deceive but not so fierce that only the deepest closers benefit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dandyman Dan and Engraved press Vega King vigorously, creating a contested early pace that burns out the leader and leaves prominent stalkers best placed.
scenarios.body: A quicker early fractions on soft ground punishes the lone leader in the closing stages and rewards horses who have settled just behind the speed; the extra stamina demands of a genuinely run seven furlongs on soft play into the hands of those with proven seven-furlong form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs after Vega King sets an overly strong gallop, leaving a vacuum for closers arriving from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A true pace collapse on soft ground opens a late lane for hold-up horses who have been restrained through the early stages; this is the scenario where Nabati's superior class and Buick's late delivery proves decisive, though it requires the tempo to be genuinely demanding enough to have softened up those ahead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves uneven or the field splits in the draw, allowing a lightly-raced unexposed runner to benefit from a favourable traffic scenario.
scenarios.body: An inexperienced runner from a favoured low draw — such as Rock Montreal from stall 7 aside, or Forbidden Fire making up ground from a high stall on a favourable outer — slips through on the rail or finds a gap as the main fancies get into traffic trouble; these horses are unproven in this company but carry low-draw or fitness angles that could flatter on the day.

watchPoints.text: Dandyman Dan's soft-ground record is 0 wins and 0 places from 5 attempts — watch to see if he travels with his usual fluency or gets outpaced early, as any struggling on the ground would confirm the Strand Scorecard danger rating is at its lower end.

Vega King's stall 2 draw means he should lead on the favoured rail, but monitor his early stride pattern — if he is pressured by Dandyman Dan or Engraved in the first furlong, the uncontested tempo assumption collapses and the race shape changes materially.

Nabati, mapping from stall 4 as a hold-up horse, needs William Buick to find a clear run in the straight; with prominent types Dandyman Dan and Engraved likely to fan wide, watch for potential traffic between them and the chasing group at the two-furlong pole.

The going is reported as Good To Soft for this race despite the race card heading of Soft — verify the actual official going at the time of running, as this distinction matters for horses (Dandyman Dan, Vega King) whose sim-going records are split between soft and good.

Kach Above's 49-day break from stall 1 makes him a horse to watch in the parade ring for signs of fitness — a well-oiled appearance from Loughnane's yard could upgrade his chance considerably given his proven 7f form.

races.name: Betfred Leger Legends Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Nyman
runners_data.note: Sole win this season came on Soft over 7f, and this 1m Good To Soft suits his stamina profile; midfield style from a neutral draw (9) means he needs a strong pace to deliver his best, which this race is likely to provide.

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: Three-year-old front-runner for Edward Bethell with a win over this trip on Good ground and soft-ground placed effort; drawn neutrally at 10 but with a favoured low-field cluster nearby, the Strand Scorecard's top pick (low confidence) and a genuine pace-setter whose fate depends on how hard Clatford presses him.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has placed consistently in soft-ground company (3P from 13 similar-going runs) but has not won in six starts showing a flat form string of 454444; midfield from draw 6 suits the style but needs the pace to really stretch.

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Scott Dixon drawn in the highly favoured stall 5, with soft-ground mile form and a placed effort at 7f on Good; Tom Scudamore takes the ride and the draw gives her every chance to track the leaders on the favoured stands-side rail.

runners_data.name: Celtic Chariot
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has won twice over this exact trip (1m Good) in recent starts and is the Strand Scorecard danger; drawn in the prime stall 1 for Adrian Nicholls and Kevin Frost, with a prominent style that gives her a major positional advantage in this contested-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Clatford
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner drawn ideally in stall 2 for Scott Dixon and Jimmy Quinn; 85 days off the track is a query, and his only form figures over 8f are limited, but his primary role is pace-setter rather than winner — his effort will shape the race for others.

runners_data.name: Little Miss India
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from 140 days off, has won over 10f and 12f on Standard and Good, stepping back to 1m here which is shorter than her best trips; Gary Bardwell rides, and the draw in favoured stall 4 is a bonus, though the trip and layoff are both concerns.

runners_data.name: Espona Bay
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent-style runner for Scott Dixon drawn wide in stall 15, working against the left-draw bias that pervades this field; has placed three times recently and has a win over 7f on Good To Soft, but the high draw negates much of her consistency.

runners_data.name: Wield
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Joseph Parr with tongue-tie applied, drawn in favoured stall 3 but posting a recent run of 072 including a tenth in Good ground; Joe Fanning is a key booking, but recent form is uninspiring and the midfield style means he relies on a strong pace.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's three-year-old has soft-going and Good To Soft form including a placed effort on Soft, but its natural hold-up tendency means it has been redistributed to midfield in the pace map — it is unlikely to access the wide rear-of-field berth it needs, tempering its chance in a contested-pace shape.

runners_data.name: Serious Look
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse who has won over 8f on Standard and placed over 10f; high draw (14) works against the left-draw bias, and while Richard Patrick rides, recent form runs of 1558 do not inspire strong confidence at this trip in soft ground.

runners_data.name: Caragio
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby trains and rides this six-year-old, who has won over 6f on Good and placed over 7f; hold-up style from stall 11 (against the draw bias) and recent 89-day absence make this a tricky proposition despite the jockey-trainer combination.

runners_data.name: Tolstoy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Brian Ellison in a recent poor-form run (-54000) including finishing 17th and 14th in Good-ground 6f handicaps; hold-up style from stall 12 (against) and a soft-going note (sim-going 1/8) suggest conditions are not prohibitive but the form is very concerning.

runners_data.name: Anthropologist
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who carries hood (headgear noted as 'p') and has run on soft going before (4th over 7f Soft in recent history); midfield from stall 8 (neutral), Sammy Jo Bell rides, but soft-going sim record of 1/15 with no wins or places is a significant negative flag.

runners_data.name: Quiet Resolve
runners_data.note: Prominent-style five-year-old for Alan Brown with Gay Kelleway aboard, drawn widest of all in stall 16 (against); has placed twice over 1m on Good and Good To Soft, but the draw almost certainly negates any positional plan in a race where early position from low stalls is at a premium.

runners_data.name: Feel The Need
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up type racing again after just 6 days; its natural position at the rear cannot be secured given the number of hold-up types in this field, so it has been moved to midfield in the pace map — discount its chance accordingly, as its soft-going record (1/8 no wins or places) adds a further concern.

races.paceDynamic: Clatford and Masaban are the two confirmed front-runners, both drawn in the favoured low-draw group (stalls 2 and 10 respectively), and their presence guarantees an early duel for the lead that will set a genuine, honest gallop on Good To Soft ground over a mile. Clatford (draw 2, favoured) will look to cross and lead from the inside, but Masaban (draw 10) has the engine and recent soft-ground form to press or match him, meaning neither will get an uncontested, easy time in front. Celtic Chariot (draw 1, favoured) and Bella Bisbee (draw 5, favoured) sit just off the pace as prominent types in the best draws, ideally positioned to track the contested lead and pounce if the front two burn each other out. This race shape — a genuinely run mile with contested early fractions on soft ground — most favours prominent racers drawn on the favoured left flank who can sit just behind the battle and quicken late; pure hold-up types will face a stiff ask unless the pace truly collapses, and the field contains more hold-up types than can realistically all settle at the rear, with Shadow Run and Feel The Need both redistributed to midfield and unlikely to secure their natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Clatford and Masaban fight for the lead and set a strong early gallop that strings the field out.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners empty each other into the straight, handing a decisive advantage to prominent types who tracked them just off the pace in the favoured low draws. Celtic Chariot and Bella Bisbee, both drawn low and prominent in style, are ideally placed to pick up the pieces as the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Masaban Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Clatford fails to cross or fades early and Masaban dictates a controlled, measured gallop.
scenarios.body: Masaban settles into a rhythm and uses its soft-ground mile form to stay on strongly, never truly tested until the straight where its stamina advantage tells. The Strand Scorecard top pick benefits from this shape most directly, and a modest pace would limit the effectiveness of hold-up horses grinding late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the front two set a fair but not punishing pace and the race resolves into a straightforward contest for horses racing in the first four or five.
scenarios.body: Horses with prominent styles drawn low — Celtic Chariot, Bella Bisbee — use their positional advantage to dictate terms from halfway and hold on against tired rivals. Nyman, drawn neutrally in stall 9 but with soft-ground form and recent winning form, could also challenge from midfield if the tempo is fair rather than furious.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is ferocious enough to set up an unusually strong late finish for genuine hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Horses like Caragio or Serious Look could theoretically close, but this scenario is discounted because Shadow Run and Feel The Need — the most natural hold-up types — are redistributed to midfield and unlikely to secure the wide position they need. Even if the pace is strong, the structural disadvantage of high draws and displaced styles makes a clean late swoop improbable.

watchPoints.text: Celtic Chariot (draw 1) is positioned perfectly to track the contested Clatford-Masaban duel from the favoured rail — if she gets a clean break, her back-to-back 1m wins make her the primary threat to Masaban.

Clatford's 85-day absence could blunt his pace-setting ability; if he fails to press Masaban from stall 2, the race dynamic shifts from contested to controlled, dramatically changing which horses are favoured.

Espona Bay's draw in stall 15 is a structural concern — Scott Dixon has three runners (Clatford, Bella Bisbee, Shadow Run) in far better positions, and if Espona Bay drops back early to find cover, the high draw will have done its damage before the race is properly underway.

Little Miss India is 140 days off the track, drops back from 10-12f to 1m, and is drawn in the favoured stall 4 — watch the market for any significant support, as a fresh and unexposed angle at this trip could catch the eye.

Shadow Run and Feel The Need are both true hold-up types squeezed into a midfield role by the volume of pace in this field — if either finds clear daylight wider out in the straight, their style-fit discount could flip, but this is an exceptional rather than expected outcome.

runners_data.name: Sale Shark
runners_data.note: Won on soft at 5f last time and has proven he handles this exact condition; draw 1 is neutral here but his early pace from a low stall is a genuine asset tracking the leaders, and his recent uplift in form makes him the most credible danger to the Strand top selection.

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien give this horse obvious claims despite a mixed record in this sphere; his best form has come at 5f on good ground and he has failed to fire on soft in one soft-ground start, making the going a mild query at this level.

runners_data.name: In The Black
runners_data.note: Won a 5f maiden on good ground last time and showed ability in the first run on soft; by nature a front-running type who cannot secure that position in this congested prominent pack, so he races out of role and must be discounted — his chance depends on a messy race producing gaps.

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners a horse with consistent midfield form including a 5f win on standard-to-slow, and his soft-ground record at 5f (4th most recently) is respectable; sits in the ideal race position if the pace is genuinely hot, needing a clear passage from draw 9.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard top selection at medium confidence; the confirmed front-runner who sets the pace and has a soft-ground second at 6f on his CV — James Doyle is a strong front-running partner and the horse's class makes him the one they all have to beat.

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy has been in good form at the meeting (T14: 4/18) and Crownbreaker has placed in a 2f-shorter race on good ground; a prominent runner who will be squeezed for position in this field, and his soft-ground run produced a 7th last time — slight going query.

runners_data.name: Flann Sunna
runners_data.note: Won twice at 6f on good ground for Crisford and Buick and is unexposed at this trip; the 43-day break is a concern first time on soft, but Buick's experience and the horse's early pace make her one of the few who might genuinely grab a prominent berth in a crowded field.

runners_data.name: Tokaido
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish; has soft-ground experience but the finishing flag makes this a difficult profile for any scenario — Amy Murphy's horse needs everything to fall right and is best treated as a fringe player.

runners_data.name: Fast Track
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner who will push Final Objective for the lead from stall 11; won three of his last five races at 5f on good ground but his soft-ground sample is limited — contested pace over 5f on today's going is the key question about whether he can sustain his effort to the line.

runners_data.name: El Floridita
runners_data.note: Has a 5f win on good and a second on good ground, plus a 6th on soft most recently; wears a visor and Rowan Scott takes the ride for Nigel Tinkler — a genuine midfield type who could benefit if the front rank folds, though the visor effect and soft-ground form are mild unknowns.

runners_data.name: Pershaada
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 5f and has a 5f win on good ground, but his last run on soft produced a 14th — a significant soft-ground concern that must be weighted heavily despite Sean Levey's presence; a prominent runner who will struggle to hold his natural position and has a going query.

runners_data.name: Ronson
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on good ground and placed at the same trip; a hold-up type who needs the pace to blow up and clear running from stall 5 — the most plausible closer if the race falls apart but entirely dependent on scenario D unfolding, which is the lowest-probability shape.

races.paceDynamic: Final Objective and Fast Track are confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from flags to the first furlong, creating a genuinely contested, honest gallop on soft ground over 5f — there will be no slow early pace to flatter hold-up horses. With five of twelve runners wanting a prominent position, the first two furlongs will see a wall of horses racing up with the pace, and any runner unable to slot in cleanly will burn energy or be forced wide. Sale Shark, Carry The Flag, Flann Sunna, Crownbreaker, and Pershaada are all vying for the same prominent berths — only two or three can genuinely hold that position, and the most likely to secure it are Sale Shark (low draw, proven soft-ground pace) and Flann Sunna (Buick, proven early speed). This race shape — a strongly-run 5f on soft ground with a congested prominent pack — overwhelmingly favours a horse with the tactical speed to sit just off the pace in a genuine rhythm and deliver a sustained, powerful finish from midfield or a high cruising position, rather than either a lone leader who can dictate or a hold-up horse dependent on the race falling apart. Note that In The Black is a natural prominent racer who has been mapped to midfield precisely because this field has more pace than it can accommodate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the contested lead between Final Objective and Fast Track burns the front two out by the 2f pole, leaving the finish to those who travelled comfortably just behind.
scenarios.body: The early duel on soft ground saps the pace-setters' finishing reserves, and the race opens up for runners who have settled in a genuine rhythm — Agamemnon and El Floridita, both natural midfield types with soft-ground form, get the strongest late sectionals.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Position Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front pair — most likely Final Objective — establishes a clear rhythm and the contested pace is honest but not truly ruinous, allowing a quality prominent runner to track and pounce.
scenarios.body: Final Objective is the Strand Scorecard top selection and has the class edge; a prominent tracker like Sale Shark, who won on soft at 5f on his last run, could peel off the pace and nail the leader close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Fast Track or Final Objective breaks cleanly, establishes a small lead, and the congestion behind causes sufficient interference to prevent a clean run from midfield chasers.
scenarios.body: Soft ground at Doncaster can reward a horse who dictates its own rhythm rather than being shuffled about, and if Final Objective avoids the traffic problems it has the class to hold on under James Doyle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that the entire prominent pack ties up and hold-up horses get a clear late run on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: Tokaido has a soft-ground flag but fades in finishes and is flagged accordingly; Ronson is the more plausible closer but needs everything to go wrong for the field — this scenario is genuinely unlikely given the redistributed nature of most hold-up types here.

watchPoints.text: Final Objective and Fast Track will go head-to-head for the lead from the off — watch whether Final Objective can establish a margin or whether Fast Track's stall 11 position forces a wider, more energy-sapping duel that compromises both.

Five prominent-style runners (Sale Shark, Carry The Flag, Flann Sunna, Crownbreaker, Pershaada) will all attempt to race in the same berths 2-3 lengths off the pace — expect significant bumping and crowding between the 2f and 3f markers where the field compacts.

In The Black's natural front-running style cannot be expressed in this field; if P J McDonald attempts to force him forward anyway, that risks overcrowding the lead and artificially inflating the early pace beyond what Final Objective or Fast Track intended.

Pershaada's last outing on soft produced a 14th — soft going is today's confirmed condition and backers should note this is a meaningful negative flag for a horse otherwise holding claims on official ratings.

Agamemnon needs a clear passage from draw 9 in a 12-runner field with heavy midfield congestion; if Daniel Tudhope secures a clean line through at the 2f pole, the horse's profile suits the dominant scenario well — watch his position at halfway.

runners_data.name: Caballo De Mar
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner drawn 6, Oisin Murphy in the saddle for George Scott; soft-going form shows 1 win from 3 similar conditions runs but he carries a fade-in-finish flag which is an obvious concern at 2m2f, and his OR-115 advantage at the top of the ratings is offset by that stamina question over this trip.

runners_data.name: Winday
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins's three-year-old won over 1m2f on good ground last time for William Buick, but his natural front-running tendency cannot be indulged here as more experienced prominent types will crowd him out early; the step up to 2m2f and soft ground are both unproven, and his low weight of 122lbs is the main asset if he settles better than expected.

runners_data.name: Queenstown
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this A P O'Brien six-year-old who won over 1m4f last time and has solid placed form at 2m-plus; prominent racer who should secure a comfortable position just off Caballo De Mar without needing to fight for it, and his sim-going record (2nd of 3 on comparable surfaces) suggests the Good to Soft poses no problem.

runners_data.name: Epic Poet
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's seven-year-old has been consistent without winning in his last five, all at 14f, and the step up to 2m2f on soft ground is a genuine question; Daniel Tudhope keeps the ride and his midfield style means he needs a proper pace to aim at, but a sim-going record of 1 from 5 on soft ground is not encouraging.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's mare holds up off the pace and has placed form on soft going (2nd and 3rd from five similar-going runs), making her one of the few runners whose style is genuinely suited to a slowly-run race that turns into a sustained stamina test; Jason Hart has ridden her to placed finishes before and the 2m2f trip looks within range based on her 2m1f run.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's six-year-old is a hold-up horse with modest recent form (best of 4th) and his sim-going record of 4th from 12 qualifying runs shows he handles the surface without excelling; Clifford Lee takes over and the wide draw in stall 8 is unlikely to hinder him over 2m2f but his OR-101 rating leaves him needing a big improvement.

runners_data.name: Ascending
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old is a front-running type by inclination but will be unable to express that here given the stronger pace horses ahead of him; the fade-in-finish warning compounds concerns about a horse whose recent form shows he has not finished in the first four across his last six starts, and the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.94 makes his chance fragile.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Sundance
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's six-year-old arrives 42 days fresh, which can suit a stayer, and his form includes wins over 1m6f on Standard going with placed form at 2m on good; a prominent racer by style who should naturally slot in behind Caballo De Mar, and P J McDonald knows the horse — the biggest query is whether his best form on Tapeta translates to soft turf over this extended trip.

races.paceDynamic: Caballo De Mar is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to pressure him from the front, he is likely to dictate a controlled, measured gallop over this 2m2f on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster. Berkshire Sundance and Queenstown will press forward prominently behind him, creating a small lead group that sets an honest but not punishing tempo — the soft-ish surface and the distance naturally moderate the early fractions. This race shape favours hold-up horses and late-finishing mid-packers who can travel economically before producing a sustained run in Doncaster's long straight, a profile that suits Peace Belle and the deeper closers more than it does the field's many nominal front-runners. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Winday and Ascending are genuine front-rank horses by inclination but are mapped to midfield here because Caballo De Mar, Queenstown, and Berkshire Sundance are likely to absorb those early slots, meaning Winday and Ascending will be forced to race further back than they prefer and their chances are accordingly discounted.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Queenstown Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Caballo De Mar sets a sustainable pace and Queenstown tracks him closely before asserting his stamina superiority in the straight.
scenarios.body: Caballo De Mar idles in front on a yielding surface, handing Queenstown an economical tow into the Doncaster straight where Ryan Moore can time his challenge to perfection; Queenstown's recent winning form over 1m6f-plus and his good-to-soft sim-going record make him the chief beneficiary of this relaxed shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Caballo De Mar Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Caballo De Mar steals an uncontested advantage and his rivals fail to pick him up when the pace lifts in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: George Scott's five-year-old sets a deceptively strong early tempo that nobody challenges, and by the time the hold-up horses ask for their effort the deficit is too great to close on soft ground; this scenario rewards those with enough tactical speed to have tracked him, primarily Berkshire Sundance who has the proven stamina at 2m-plus.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or riders misjudge the tempo, leaving a sprint finish that plays into the hands of fresh-finishing hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Peace Belle and Beylerbeyi, both held up off the pace, get the clean run they need in the straight and produce late surges that overhaul a tiring lead group; Peace Belle's course form and soft-going record give her an edge in this shape, and Beylerbeyi's hold-up style means he always has a chance if the race sets up genuinely late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Ascending or Winday overcomes their redistribution and forces a contested early gallop that breaks the race apart mid-race.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected pace burns off Caballo De Mar and fragments the field into a race of attrition, opening the door for the most robust stayer to grind it out; Epic Poet, with his consistent placed form over 14f in good ground and a proven ability to stay competitive in attritional races, could pick up pieces ahead of Peace Belle.

watchPoints.text: Watch Queenstown's early position — if Ryan Moore settles him smoothly in second or third behind Caballo De Mar without expending energy, he controls his own destiny in the straight and becomes very difficult to peg back.

Watch Caballo De Mar's sectionals from the halfway point — his fade-in-finish flag means if he has been allowed to idle and then quicken briefly he could empty late, gifting a free sprint to those immediately behind him.

Watch Winday and Ascending in the early stages — if either manages to force their way to prominent positions ahead of where they are mapped, the pace dynamic changes and the race could be run faster than expected, increasing the danger to the lead horses.

Watch Peace Belle's run turning into the straight — she needs a clear passage from her wide draw in stall 5 and if Jason Hart finds daylight early in the home straight on soft ground her stamina profile could produce a strong late surge.

Watch Berkshire Sundance's freshness — 42 days off can sharpen a stayer, and if he travels strongly in the prominent group for Balding and McDonald the combination of fitness from a break and proven stamina at 2m-plus makes him a quiet threat if the pace proves modest.

runners_data.name: Salamanca City
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's five-year-old mare has soft-ground and 1m2f-1m4f form (1W2P in 6 similar-going runs) and sits in a midfield role that suits a race likely to be run at a genuine clip; carries 138lbs which is the biggest burden in the field and could blunt her finishing kick if the ground is genuinely testing.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's six-year-old is the Strand Scorecard's top selection and has shown a pattern of winning at 1m2f-1m4f on good ground with two places in soft — the hold-up style fits the anticipated late-run scenario perfectly; Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim reduces the burden meaningfully and the 13-day turnaround is not a concern given that trainer's recent form.

runners_data.name: Room Fourteen
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes the ride on this lightly-weighted 3yo, who has an excellent recent form string of 5 wins/places in her last 6 outings, all at 1m2f on good ground; the step to 1m4f on softer going is an unknown (no soft-ground history), and 42 days off makes her freshness a marginal concern, though Fanshawe handles seasonal horses well.

runners_data.name: Ruby Wedding
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy on an Andrew Balding three-year-old who ran well at 1m2f on Good To Soft (1 win from 7 soft runs) and is mapped as a prominent runner — she could leverage a clean position just off the contested leaders; the 125lb weight and stepping up from 1m1f-1m2f trips to 1m4f is the primary trip question.

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso

runners_data.name: Nochebuena
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is one of the two confirmed front-runners who will create the contested early pace; won at 1m2f in Soft and placed twice in Soft conditions, but a 63-day absence raises fitness questions and being embroiled in a pace duel over 1m4f on softish ground could drain stamina reserves entirely.

runners_data.name: Aequitas
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old won at 1m2f on good but has been absent for 307 days, finishing 16th and 11th in her last two starts — a layoff of this magnitude means form is essentially unknown on reappearance; Daniel Tudhope is a useful booking but this runner asks a lot of trust from punters.

runners_data.name: Golden Muse
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's three-year-old has a strong form record (3 wins from 5 recent runs) but all on Standard or good surfaces — zero soft-ground form whatsoever is a significant flag on Good To Soft ground at Doncaster; as the other confirmed front-runner, she will have to work from the wide draw (10) to get across, costing extra energy before a stride has been run in anger.

runners_data.name: Bint Al Daar
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's six-year-old carries a visor marker and her soft-going form is uninspiring (11th in last soft run), with a form string of 158790 suggesting a horse running below her best; Joanna Mason picks up the ride but the OR of 70 and recent form make this look like a run for education or fitness rather than a winning contender.

races.paceDynamic: Nochebuena and Golden Muse are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 1m4f trip on Good To Soft ground at Doncaster. That duel is likely to produce an honest, pressured gallop rather than a sedate tempo, meaning neither can dictate entirely on their own terms and energy will be expended early. The Good To Soft surface at Doncaster — despite the official card notation — rewards stamina and will stretch the field out, amplifying the cost of any early battle for supremacy. This contested pace shape strongly favours hold-up and midfield horses with proven stamina on soft-side ground, as the front pair are likely to soften each other up before the final turn, handing the initiative to those arriving late with a sustained run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Nochebuena and Golden Muse burn each other off at a strong gallop, setting up a strong-finishing run from behind.
scenarios.body: The two leaders drain each other's reserves through the first mile, leaving the race wide open for hold-up and midfield runners to sweep past the tiring principals in the straight; Good To Soft ground rewards those who conserve energy and deliver a single sustained effort late. Green Sky and Silver Lake, both hold-up horses with soft-ground form, are ideally positioned to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong but not punishing enough to fully stop the prominent types, allowing a stalker just off the leaders to pounce.
scenarios.body: Ruby Wedding or Thatwilldoso, tracking the pace just behind the duelling leaders, could use their prominent position to kick for home turning in before the hold-up horses close the gap; this shape suits horses who get a clean sit in fourth or fifth and don't get trapped wide. The Good To Soft surface doesn't punish prominent runners unduly at this trip as long as they haven't had to fight for position early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two lead duellists — most likely Nochebuena — establishes a fractional advantage early and the pace proves steadier than expected.
scenarios.body: Nochebuena has proven soft-ground stamina at 1m2f-1m4f and, ridden conservatively by Jason Hart, could slot in front without burning out; if Golden Muse fails to match strides or settles for second-in-command, the gallop becomes manageable and the leader gets to control their own rhythm. Ralph Beckett's consistent form and Nochebuena's record of placing in soft conditions give this scenario genuine, if secondary, credibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Class Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race into a tactical crawl despite the two leaders, turning the finish into a sprint test.
scenarios.body: Salamanca City and Aequitas, both midfield types carrying significant weight, would be better positioned than most in a muddled-tempo race that becomes a sprint from 2f out; however, Aequitas has a 307-day absence and soft-ground query, making this shape the least reliable for producing a clean result. This is a low-probability scenario because two genuine front-runners make a genuine crawl almost impossible.

watchPoints.text: Golden Muse (draw 10) will need to cross from the outside to secure her front-running position — if Nochebuena contests that move aggressively from draw 2, both may use up significant energy before the race has properly begun, compressing the advantage of the prominent stalkers.

Thatwilldoso has a notably poor record on soft-side going (7th of 8 soft runs, 1W3P only on good) — if the ground deteriorates further through the card, her chances reduce markedly despite her solid recent form on good ground.

Aequitas has been absent for 307 days and posted poor recent turf figures (16th, 11th) — any dramatic market move toward her should be treated cautiously unless a convincing gallops report is in circulation, as trainer O'Meara's 14-day strike rate of 5/55 is uninspiring.

Room Fourteen has no soft-ground history at all — if the going description of Good To Soft proves to be on the soft end of that range (as the card listing suggests possible), her form profile is built entirely on good ground and a stamina question at 1m4f compounds the uncertainty.

Green Sky's claim-assisted 128lb burden, combined with a 13-day turnaround, means Charlie Tucker's 7lb allowance is doing real carrying work — watch whether the claim is ultimately retained or if there is a late jockey change, as that would alter the weight dynamic for the Strand Scorecard's top selection.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Toledo
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner for Clive Cox and P J McDonald; has soft-going experience and won over 6f on good, but faces fierce early competition for the lead and the soft ground could blunt its stamina if it burns fuel in a pace war.

runners_data.name: Bear Lee
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard danger; Michael & David Easterby's hold-up runner has a win on soft and consistent placed form at this trip, drawn low in stall 1 which adds positional complexity, but the projected strong pace is tailor-made for a horse coming from off it.

runners_data.name: Washington Royale
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with a recent win on soft going (1/6f/SOF) for Michael Appleby; the soft-ground win is the key qualifier and a prominent pitch just off the pace suits perfectly if the front-runners soften each other up.

runners_data.name: Baddaddan
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's prominent racer enters off a 20-day break; the lone previous form on soft is a 14th on good ground and the form string tails off sharply with a last-time-out 0, making this a hard one to trust in demanding conditions.

runners_data.name: Super Tuscan
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's consistent prominent type with a win on good and multiple placed efforts at 6f; the 7-lb claimer Oliver Carmichael rides, which is a positive in terms of weight, though the soft going and pace scenario ask genuine questions of stamina.

runners_data.name: Wait Geordie

runners_data.name: Beresford Gap

runners_data.name: Sir Sirius

runners_data.name: Innichen

runners_data.name: Sue's Last Chance

runners_data.name: Fasthope
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner has genuine soft-ground form (2/5 in sim-going) and won over 6f on good last time; a natural prominent racer who will find herself shuffled wider than preferred given the volume of pace ahead — the style-fit discount (0.94) is noted and her chance depends on whether she can still access a prominent pitch from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's progressive filly has a solid record (431346) and a win at 6f on good; the headgear flag (hg:ht) and high draw in stall 16 compound the challenge of her being a natural prominent type in a field overloaded with pace — she will likely find herself operating further off the speed than ideal, softening her prospects.

races.paceDynamic: Pride Of Toledo, Wait Geordie, Beresford Gap, Sir Sirius, and Sue's Last Chance all profile as genuine front-runners, guaranteeing a fierce early gallop on Good To Soft ground over 6f at Doncaster — this is not a contested pace scenario, it is a war of attrition from the first stride. The soft underfoot conditions will amplify the stamina test, meaning those committed to leading will burn each other out by halfway, leaving the race wide open for horses racing in behind to pick up the pieces. This shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types with genuine stamina and soft-ground form who can settle in the slipstream and produce a sustained late drive — hold-up finishers operating off a true pace also enter the picture. The field contains more prominent and front-running types than can all secure their preferred position; Fern Clyde and Fasthope are both natural prominent racers who are likely to be shuffled back by the sheer volume of pace ahead and will find themselves racing further off the speed than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners burn each other out by the 3f pole, leaving prominent-to-midfield settlers to sweep through.
scenarios.body: The fierce early gallop on soft ground drains the leaders entering the straight, and horses who were able to cover the pace from a position just off it are perfectly placed to quicken into the gap; Doncaster's straight 6f rewards that sustained drive to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace setters settles better than rivals and conserves enough energy to hold the late challenge.
scenarios.body: With multiple rivals keen to lead, a horse that naturally finds a rhythm slightly off the very front edge rather than the centrepiece of the duel can steal a march into the straight and prove too far gone; Pride Of Toledo, with Clive Cox's soft-ground record, is the best candidate to execute this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so scorching that even prominent settlers are compromised and genuine hold-up horses finish best of all.
scenarios.body: A truly blistering early tempo can see the entire prominent pack weaken, allowing Innichen and Bear Lee to weave through a wall of tired horses late; Bear Lee in particular has the soft-ground profile and hold-up style to maximise this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Moderate, Midfield Squeeze
scenarios.trigger: If early aggression is tempered by the going and the field bunches, creating a messy scenario where no clear flow emerges.
scenarios.body: A compressed, slowly-run scenario suits a horse with a sharp turn of foot who can pounce from mid-division; Launch Sequence and Henley On Thames carry the class and jockey quality to exploit a tactical race, though this shape is less likely given the volume of confirmed pace.

watchPoints.text: Pride Of Toledo, Wait Geordie, Beresford Gap, Sir Sirius, and Sue's Last Chance all seek to lead — watch the opening furlong for an explosive pace war that could leave the entire front rank spent by halfway.

Fern Clyde and Fasthope are natural prominent racers drawn in stalls 15 and 16; watch whether either can work forward to a prominent position or whether the sheer number of speed horses forces them to settle much further back than intended, materially reducing their chances.

Bear Lee is drawn in stall 1 — watch whether Joanna Mason can navigate cleanly from the lowest draw in a 16-runner field without getting squeezed or forced to race wide as horses fan across the track.

Launch Sequence is fitted with a hood (hg:p) and represents K R Burke's string in fine form (T14: 13/42); watch for a forward move from midfield if the pace truly collapses, as James Doyle will be looking to exploit any late gaps.

The going report lists this race as Good To Soft despite the narrative SOFT designation — watch the official going board at the track, as any further softening into the day would increase the stamina premium and further favour horses with proven soft-ground records such as Washington Royale and Bear Lee.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly, On The Inlet, Director's Cut, Canvas, and Ziata all have front-running profiles, guaranteeing a fierce early battle for supremacy on this flat 1m2f Doncaster circuit in Good To Soft conditions — the pace will be genuine from the first stride, not manufactured. With five horses competing for the early lead, at least two or three will be forced to burn excess energy before halfway, softening the field for those travelling more economically behind. The soft-ish ground amplifies stamina demands, meaning any horse unable to switch off after a contested early pace will fade badly in the straight. This race shape unequivocally favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can settle in behind the carnage, conserve energy through the middle stages, and then produce a sustained finish — pure hold-up horses who lack a turn of foot on soft ground are the chief losers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the five-way front-running battle burns itself out leaving the field strung out by halfway, allowing midfield stalkers to mow down the stragglers in the straight.
scenarios.body: The contested early lead on soft ground drains the front runners, and horses like Optician and Something Splendid, travelling mid-pack with cover, arrive with fresh legs in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Director's Cut or On The Inlet — refuses to be pressured and establishes a clear rhythm while rivals over-race.
scenarios.body: That horse controls the tempo, keeps the pace honest but not suicidal, and the race becomes a test of class rather than pure stamina, rewarding the horse that led with the most residual ability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Grab It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fractures the early leaders but a prominent settler like Something Splendid or Everyoneknowsadave tracks close enough to the action and kicks at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: These horses get the best of both worlds — not burning energy in the early scrap but close enough to pounce before hold-up horses can wind up their challenge on soft ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly suicidal and the winner comes from the very back of the field with Fans Favourite or Spirit Genie delivering a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: This requires a near-record collapse in the front rank and a clear passage through traffic, which is unlikely with 19 runners on a wide flat course where midfielders often pinch the prize first.

watchPoints.text: Canvas and Ziata are both confirmed or likely faders over this trip on soft ground — if either fires into an early lead alongside Highland Olly and On The Inlet, the pace will be genuinely suicidal and closers could dominate from a furlong out.

Fans Favourite with Oisin Murphy aboard carries major jockey significance — if Murphy rides aggressively rather than waiting, a horse with three soft-ground wins could steal this from a prominent position, catching the market cold at a big price.

Reveur's 126-day layoff and unknown soft-ground preference is a wildcard; David O'Meara runners returning fresh with Tudhope booked after a break often show their hand early in the market, so watch any late price movement as a key signal.

Something Splendid (draw 2) is the Strand Scorecard danger — Tom Marquand will need to negotiate early traffic from a low draw without getting caught in the front-running battle; if he can slot comfortably in third or fourth, the horse's soft-ground record makes it extremely dangerous.

With 19 runners and MINIMAL draw bias favouring middle stalls, horses drawn in the high teens (Illy's Roo 19, Fans Favourite 17, Ziata 18) will need to find a clear passage through the field in the straight — a congested finish is likely and in-running positioning will be decisive.
